rule.bounds: per positive src/dst pair: floor(src_start)<window_end; ceil(dst_end)>window_start; and ceil(src_end)>window_start only for certified remote-delivery completion
rule.rounding: outward to the same public clock resolution in every condition
rule.aggregation: union of still-possible sources; never use destination start as packet lower bound
rule.mapping: last application transmission START window end; preserve destination-end capture guard
rule.unknown: missing records and uncovered future remain possible; empty queue is not final completion
rule.scope: offline application operation candidates, not protocol retirement or causal business loss

compact_information.process: one pass over nonzero relation rows, then one lookup per candidate operation/port; not an online or SRAM cost

offline.interpretation: All comparisons are retrospective. Ideal exclusions use the sealed future capture; endpoints are also complete offline observations.

limitations: FIFO known set complete, upstream waiting only partially captured; unconfirmed is not automatically false.
Positive queue without known application remains unknown, not automatically protocol.
Related windows and nested request records are not independent statistical samples.

audit.distinction: Remote data delivery bounds outgoing application data/status; ACK/credit and protocol retirement are not bounded by operator end. Local read completion alone is ineligible.

rule.hypothesis: An application packet waiting at an outlet must start transmission in a later compatible nonzero public packet window.
rule.envelope: Intersect positive packet windows with each positive source/destination temporal envelope; union sources. The last compatible window end is a conservative upper bound, not an estimated last application packet.
rule.safe_unknown: Missing windows or destination completion beyond capture cannot certify a final boundary.
rule.control: All protocol/metadata traffic remains eligible public traffic; do not subtract logical payload from wire bytes.
rule.alternative: If other application or protocol traffic fills all temporal opportunities, counters cannot tighten these bounds.
rule.scope: One fixed simple rule; a failed attempt does not prove universal unidentifiability.

review_scope: 80 windows at 0-40 us; same 1000 ns precision and fixed rule hashes. This historically studied nested request subset is not an independent holdout.
